soundness_requirements: SAME GROUND TRUTH: C1-full, C1-nohardening, and C2-naive must all be scored against the IDENTICAL label set. The detection harness (A) scores per-event against experiment/corpus/ground-truth/labels.jsonl; the C3-Elastic baseline (harness B) was scored per-playbook against .alerts-security.alerts-default over the 10 new attack runs. These are two DIFFERENT ground-truth granularities and label spaces. You cannot place C3 in the same P/R/F2 table as C1-full unless both are re-projected onto one common ground truth and one common scoring function. Mixing them is the single biggest confound.

SAME TELEMETRY WINDOW: every condition must read from the same Sysmon/Elastic index over the same execution window. C1-full/C2/C1-nohardening must query the same time range the C3 baseline used on the new runs, or be explicitly scoped to a different (older) corpus and reported as such. Do not compare C1-full on the new runs against C2/C1-nohardening numbers carried over from the May archive at a different telemetry state.

SAME EVENT SET / SAME N: all conditions classify the same filtered event population (execution_success=true AND executed=true), grouped identically, with identical seed for ordering. If C1-full is scoped to a subset (cost), then C2-naive and C1-nohardening MUST be re-scored on that exact same subset, not the full set. A subset-vs-full comparison is an automatic confound.

IDENTICAL SCORING: one compute_metrics.py invocation, same beta (F2, beta=2.0 per config), same malicious/benign mapping, same not_evaluated handling. not_evaluated predictions must be counted identically across conditions (either all as FN or all excluded) — never silently dropped for one condition and counted for another.

GOVERNANCE IS THE ONLY MANIPULATED VARIABLE: C1-full vs C1-nohardening vs C2-naive must differ ONLY in the governance/prompt layer (M1-M5 + M3 framework present / partially disabled / absent). Same model, same temperature/seed, same ES query template, same retry policy. If C1-full uses a different model snapshot (skill says claude-opus-4-6) than the re-scored baselines, the delta is confounded by model version, not governance — pin one model for the whole matrix.

CONTAMINATION SEPARATION: the clean detection matrix (no injection) and the adversarial matrix (under injection) must be reported as two distinct experiments. Do not blend per-attack-burst / steganographic injection runs into the clean P/R/F2 numbers. The clean matrix establishes baseline detection competence; the adversarial matrix establishes resilience. Conflating them inflates or deflates both.

PER-CONDITION REPLICATION + CI: if cost forces 1 run/condition for C1-full, the comparison cannot rest on a single point estimate. Either run >=3 seeds for C1-full, or report the single run with the per-event bootstrap CI (bootstrap_ci.py, B=10000) already used for C3 reproducibility, and state the n=1 limitation explicitly. A bare single-run delta is rejectable.
key_contribution_metric: The headline contribution is NOT raw detection quality (P/R/F2) — that is table-stakes context. The thesis (resilience to adversarial log injection) is proven by the ADVERSARIAL CONTRAST: Attack Success Rate (ASR = misclassified-malicious / N) and Non-Attributed Success Rate (NASR = attack_success AND injection_detected==false) measured under the A1 (memory-poisoning: suppress/misdirect) and A2 (malfunction-amplification: contradictory/exhaustion) injection families, with the SAME injected events scored across conditions. The load-bearing single number is the ASR delta: C1-full ASR should be a small fraction of C2-naive ASR (the skill's worked example: C2-naive a2-exhaustion ASR=0.500 vs C1-full ~0.083, a ~6x reduction), and NASR should collapse toward 0 for C1-full because M3/M5 flag the injection (injection_detected=true) while C2-naive silently complies. The C1-deltaM2 ablation isolates which mechanism does the work. Concretely the paper must show: (1) clean detection: C1-full F2 >= C2-naive (governance does not cost detection quality), AND (2) under injection: C1-full ASR << C2-naive ASR and C1-full NASR ~ 0 while C2-naive NASR is high. Contribution = stability under contamination, not peak F2 on clean data. If the only result is 'C1-full has higher F2 on clean logs,' the dissertation has not demonstrated its stated thesis and a reviewer will say so.
harness_recommendation: Use BOTH harnesses, for two different claims, and do not substitute one for the other. (1) For the CLEAN detection matrix (C1-full vs C1-nohardening vs C2-naive vs C3-Elastic), the correct unit depends on the claim: C3-Elastic was produced per-PLAYBOOK against .alerts (harness B), so to place C3 in the same table every condition must be scored at the per-playbook/per-detection-window granularity — meaning C1/C2 per-event predictions must be aggregated up to a per-playbook detection decision before scoring, OR C3 must be re-projected down to per-event. Per-EVENT (harness A) is the scientifically cleaner unit because it is the native ground truth (labels.jsonl) and gives the LLM conditions their fairest, highest-resolution score; but then C3 cannot share that table without re-projection and must instead appear in a separate per-playbook table with an explicit note. RECOMMENDATION: report the LLM conditions (C1-full/C1-nohardening/C2-naive) head-to-head PER-EVENT via harness A (apples-to-apples, same labels, isolates governance), and report C3-Elastic PER-PLAYBOOK in its own row/table with the granularity difference stated — never silently merged. (2) For the RESILIENCE claim (the actual thesis), the correct harness is the ADVERSARIAL trial harness (hunt-adversarial: per-injected-event ASR/NASR), per-event, because injection resistance is an event-level property of each classification decision — per-playbook aggregation would hide exactly the per-attack-burst injection effect the thesis is about. Bottom line: per-event for the governance head-to-head and for resilience; per-playbook only for the C3 SIEM cross-reference, clearly labeled as a different unit.
reviewer_rejection_risks: Apples-to-oranges table: C3 scored per-playbook on the new runs while C1/C2 scored per-event on a different corpus, presented in one P/R/F2 table as if comparable. Most likely single cause of a reject.

Carried-over baselines: re-scoring only C1-full on the new runs but pulling C2-naive / C1-nohardening numbers from the May archive (different telemetry state, possibly different model) into the same comparison — invalidates every delta.

Thesis-evidence mismatch: claiming 'resilient to adversarial log injection' in the title/abstract but the Results only contain clean-corpus P/R/F2 and no ASR/NASR-under-injection contrast. The central claim would be unsupported by the central experiment.

n=1 with no uncertainty: a single C1-full run reported as a point estimate with no CI / no replication, while the rest of the paper (C3 reproducibility) used B=10000 bootstrap. Inconsistent rigor invites rejection of the headline result specifically.

Model-version confound: C1-full run with a newer/older model than the re-scored baselines, so the governance delta is entangled with model capability. Must pin one model across the entire matrix and state it.

Fabrication / non-reproducibility: any number that cannot be regenerated from artifacts under results/. Hard constraint from the brief — single fastest path to a desk-reject in a reproducibility-themed dissertation.

Leakage / unfair baseline: if the C1-full prompt embeds ground-truth-shaped hints (e.g., the M3 framework or KB seeded with answers) that C2-naive lacks beyond the governance manipulation itself, the comparison is contaminated. The only legitimate difference must be the governance layer.
Selective subset: scoping C1-full to a convenient subset of LOLBins/runs that flatters governance while baselines are scored on the full set, or cherry-picking which of the 10 runs C1-full sees.
conditions: Pin ONE model for the entire C1-full / C1-nohardening / C2-naive matrix and record it in every metadata.json; do not mix the skill-default claude-opus-4-6 with whatever runs now.
Re-score C2-naive AND C1-nohardening on the SAME run(s)/subset and SAME telemetry window as C1-full — no archive carry-over into the head-to-head table.
Report the LLM conditions per-event (harness A) in one table; report C3-Elastic per-playbook (harness B) in a separate, explicitly-labeled table; never merge granularities silently.

Run the adversarial harness (A1 suppress/misdirect, A2 contradictory/exhaustion) for at least C1-full and C2-naive (and C1-deltaM2 for mechanism attribution) and make the ASR/NASR contrast the headline Results figure — the clean matrix is supporting context, not the thesis evidence.
If C1-full is n=1 per condition due to LLM cost, attach the per-event bootstrap CI (B=10000) and state the single-run limitation explicitly in both Results and Limitations.

Confirm ground-truth labels exist for the new attack runs at the granularity each harness scores; if labels.jsonl does not cover the new runs, either generate them deterministically or scope C1-full to the corpus the labels DO cover and report that scope honestly.

Verify the only difference between C1-full and C2-naive prompts is the governance layer (M1-M5 + M3 framework) — same ES query template, same retry/not_evaluated handling, no answer leakage in either prompt.
key_question_for_managers: Do per-event ground-truth labels (labels.jsonl) actually cover the 10 NEW attack runs, or only the older corpus? If only the old corpus, then C1-full on the new runs cannot be scored per-event against existing labels, and the entire matrix must either (a) re-run C1-full on the labelled corpus, or (b) build new per-event labels for the new runs — which decision are we taking, and does C3-Elastic's per-playbook scoring even share a ground truth with the per-event LLM conditions, or are we silently comparing two different label spaces?
